The React frontend obtains\na Supabase access token through a managed sign-in flow, and the handwritten Express API validates\nthat identity using `@supabase/supabase-js`.\n\nThe frontend may use Supabase for authentication, but application data remains behind the handwritten backend API.\n\nAfter verification, the backend creates or synchronizes a provider-neutral `app_user` record and\nloads role, submitter-approval state, disabled state, and granted competition scopes from\nPostgreSQL. Authentication alone never grants or changes those values.\n\nReusable backend policies protect administrator routes, approved-submitter routes, and target\ncompetition scope. Missing or invalid credentials receive `401`; authenticated accounts that fail\na policy receive a consistent, non-disclosing `403`. Public read routes do not use authentication.\n\nSee:\n\n- [Authentication, accounts and authorisation](authentication.md)\n- [Authentication provider comparison](auth-provider-comparison.md)\n\n## Input and data protection\n\n- Validate all request bodies, files, parameters, and query strings.\n- Apply upload size/type limits and reject invalid files with actionable messages.\n- Use transactions and uniqueness constraints for idempotent batch ingestion.\n- Parameterise database queries.\n- Store secrets in deployment secret stores, never source control.\n- Minimise personal data and define deletion/retention behaviour.\n\n## API protection\n\n- Enforce HTTPS in deployed environments.\n- Apply safe CORS rules rather than allowing arbitrary origins in production.\n- Add rate limits and quotas before issuing public consumer keys.\n- Use timeouts, retries with limits, and circuit-breaking/fallback behaviour for external APIs.\n- Return safe error messages and structured internal logs.\n\n## Verification\n\nSecurity review must include automated dependency scanning, route-level authorisation tests, negative validation tests, secret scanning, deployment review, and manual threat-model updates for major features.\n\n## Database credentials\n\n- The hosted PostgreSQL connection string is a secret. It lives only in the\n  ignored `apps/backend/.env` locally, and in the deployment secret store\n  otherwise. It must never appear in an issue, a Pull Request, a commit or a group\n  chat.\n- The connection uses TLS with certificate verification enabled, against the\n  authority certificate committed at `apps/backend/certs/supabase-ca.crt`.\n  Certificate verification must not be disabled to resolve a connection error.\n- All six team members hold owner access on the hosted project. Schema changes are\n  therefore applied only through committed migrations, never through the\n  provider's SQL editor, so that the database and the migration history cannot\n  diverge without record.\n- If the connection string is exposed, rotate the database password from the\n  provider dashboard, update the deployment secret store, and notify the team. The\n  exposed value must be treated as compromised even if the exposure appears\n  contained.\n- The generated Data API is disabled on the instance. It must not be enabled, and\n  the Supabase client library must not be added to any workspace.\n\n## AI Declaration\n\nThe authentication and authorization status was updated with the assistance of\nCodex[GPT-5.6 Sol].\n\r\n\n===== auth authorization sections =====\r\nscope from the frontend.\r\n\r\nThe profile response combines the verified identity with server-owned application state:\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\r\n  \"user\": {\r\n    \"id\": \"42\",\r\n    \"subject\": \"<supabase-user-id>\",\r\n    \"displayName\": \"Example User\",\r\n    \"role\": \"viewer\",\r\n    \"approvalState\": \"approved\",\r\n    \"competitionIds\": [\"7\", \"12\"]\r\n  }\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\nThe API does not trust an unverified, manually decoded token.\r\n\r\n## Application authorisation model\r\n\r\nRoles and submission approval are deliberately separate:\r\n\r\n- `viewer` is the default role;\r\n- `administrator` is required by administrator-only middleware;\r\n- `not_requested`, `pending`, `approved`, and `rejected` describe submitter approval; and\r\n- an approved submitter must also have a `submitter_competition_scope` row for the target\r\n  competition.\r\n\r\n### Requesting submitter access\r\n\r\nAuthentication does not itself grant submission permission. An authenticated application account may explicitly request submitter access through:\r\n\r\n```http\r\nPOST /api/v1/submitter-access-requests\r\nAuthorization: Bearer <supabase-access-token>\r\n```\r\n\r\nThe backend uses the authenticated and synchronized `app_user` account rather than accepting an account identifier from the client.\r\n\r\nEligible state transitions are:\r\n\r\n```text\r\nnot_requested -> pending\r\nrejected      -> pending\r\n```\r\n\r\nAn existing `pending` request is rejected with `409 Conflict`, preventing duplicate active requests.\r\n\r\nAn `approved` submitter is also rejected with `409 Conflict` because no additional request is necessary.\r\n\r\nThe state transition is performed with a conditional PostgreSQL update so that concurrent duplicate requests cannot both create a new active request.\r\n\r\nThe signed-in Account page loads `/api/v1/auth/me` whenever it mounts and displays the persisted\r\nstate. `not_requested` and `rejected` accounts receive the request action, `pending` accounts see an\r\nawaiting-review state without another action, and `approved` accounts receive a link to the scoped\r\n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TEMPORARY_ACCESS_TOKEN\" `\r\n  http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/v1/auth/me\r\n```\r\n\r\nExpected result:\r\n\r\n```text\r\nHTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\n```\r\n\r\nThe response must contain the synchronized application profile. Verify role, approval and scope\r\nagainst the database rather than against token claims or frontend state.\r\n\r\nReplace the token immediately after use and clear it from shell history where practical. Never include the real token in test evidence.\r\n\r\n## Automated tests\r\n\r\nThe backend tests cover:\r\n\r\n1. missing, invalid and expired bearer tokens return `401`;\r\n2. a valid token synchronizes and returns the application profile;\r\n3. a disabled account and denied role/approval/scope checks return `403`;\r\n4. a normal signed-in user cannot access administrator or upload policies;\r\n5. an approved in-scope submitter passes upload policies;\r\n6. an approved out-of-scope submitter is denied;\r\n7. an administrator passes administrator policy; and\r\n8. public reads do not invoke authentication.\r\n\r\nThe test application injects a mock verifier. Automated tests therefore do not require live Supabase credentials or contact the hosted Auth service.\r\n\r\nThe manual development proof separately exercises the real `supabase.auth.getUser()` validation path.\r\n\r\nRun the backend checks with:\r\n\r\n```powershell\r\nnpm.cmd run typecheck --workspace @sport-analytics/backend\r\nnpm.cmd run lint --workspace @sport-analytics/backend\r\nnpm.cmd test --workspace @sport-analytics/backend\r\nnpm.cmd run build --workspace @sport-analytics/backend\r\n```\r\n\r\n## Local Supabase support\r\n\r\nSupabase provides a CLI that can run the database, Auth service and supporting services locally.\r\n\r\nA project-scoped setup uses:\r\n\r\n```powershell\r\nnpm.cmd install --save-dev supabase\r\nnpx.cmd supabase init\r\nnpx.cmd supabase start\r\n\r\n## Authentication versus authorisation\r\n\r\nAuthentication answers:\r\n\r\n> Who is making this request?\r\n\r\nAuthorisation answers:\r\n\r\n> What is this identity allowed to do?\r\n\r\nA valid Supabase identity does not automatically grant:\r\n\r\n- administrator access;\r\n- approved-submitter status;\r\n- competition access;\r\n- season or fixture access;\r\n- event submission rights;\r\n- sport-specific permissions.\r\n\r\nThe backend enforces those rules from application database state. It should only be introduced when asynchronous work is implemented; it is not required for the initial scaffold.\r\n\r\n## Components and responsibilities\r\n\r\n### React frontend\r\n\r\n- Render accessible and responsive user journeys.\r\n- Collect and perform user-friendly client-side validation.\r\n- Call only documented backend endpoints for application data.\r\n- Handle loading, empty, error, unauthorised, and offline/unreachable states.\r\n- Never contain database credentials or authoritative business rules.\r\n\r\n### Node.js backend\r\n\r\n- Expose the versioned hand-written HTTP API.\r\n- Validate input and authenticate/authorise protected requests.\r\n- Enforce submitter scope, review workflows, traceability, and business rules.\r\n- Read and write the database through server-side repositories.\r\n- Call the external API while controlling credentials, retries, timeouts, and failure handling.\r\n- Produce stable error responses, logs, metrics, and audit evidence.\r\n\r\n### Shared contracts package\r\n\r\n- Hold request/response and event schemas shared across applications.\r\n- Provide TypeScript types derived from validation schemas.\r\n- Contain no database access, secrets, business logic, or authorisation decisions.\r\n\r\n### Database\r\n\r\n- Store source event data, submissions, review/correction history, definitions, derived results, and releases.\r\n- Enforce integrity with constraints and transactions.\r\n- Support traceability and efficient filtered queries through deliberate indexes.\r\n\r\n### Documentation site\r\n\r\n- Publish architecture, API, database, setup, testing, dependencies, security, deployment, methodology, and AI-use documentation.\r\n- Remain publicly accessible without requiring an account.\r\n\r\n## Data flow\r\n\r\n1. An account with the `submitter` or `admin` role uploads or sends event data to the backend API.\r\n2. The backend authenticates the submitter and checks their authorised competition scope.\r\n3. The backend validates the payload against the versioned event schema.\r\n4. Valid data is staged or stored transactionally; invalid data returns actionable errors.\r\n5. Accepted event changes trigger only the dependent statistic calculations.\r\n6. Published API responses and dataset releases retain provenance to submissions, events, and definition versions.\r\n7. The frontend and external consumers obtain data from the backend API, never directly from generated database endpoints.\r\n\r\n## Security boundaries\r\n\r\n- Treat all browser and external-consumer input as untrusted.\r\n- Keep provider secrets, database credentials, external API keys, and service tokens server-side.\r\n- Use an established authentication provider/library; do not create password hashing, reset tokens, or session cryptography from scratch.\r\n- Authorise every protected route based on backend-verified identity and role/scope.\r\n- Rate-limit public/consumer endpoints before exposing them broadly.\r\n- Do not log credentials, tokens, full sensitive payloads, or unnecessary personal data.\r\n\r\n## Deployment boundaries\r\n\r\nThe frontend, backend, database, and documentation site must be independently deployable. The initial Azure deployment design is documented under `infra/azure/` and must be updated once exact services are selected and tested.\r\n\r\n## Trade-offs\r\n\r\nA monorepo simplifies shared tooling, atomic Pull Requests, and contracts while preserving separate deployable applications. The folder boundaries, backend-only database rule, and CI checks must be enforced during review.\r\n# System architecture and development roadmap\r\n\r\n**Status:** Target architecture; foundation components are implemented, while later-tier\r\ncomponents are explicitly marked as planned.  \r\n**Related issues:** #38, #73\r\n**Last updated:** 12 August 2026\r\n\r\n## 1. Purpose and architectural principles\r\n\r\nThe Sport Analytics Tool is an event-driven cricket analytics platform. It accepts\r\ntraceable match-event submissions, validates and stores accepted events, derives statistics\r\nfrom those events, and publishes results through a web application, dataset exports, and a\r\nversioned HTTP API.\r\n\r\nThe design follows these principles:\r\n\r\n1. The React frontend and Express backend are separate applications and separate deployment\r\n   units. They communicate through the documented HTTP API.\r\n2. The handwritten backend is the only application-data boundary. The frontend and external\r\n   consumers never use database-generated REST or GraphQL endpoints.\r\n3. PostgreSQL event records are the source of truth. Published statistics are derived values,\r\n   not independently entered totals.\r\n4. Authentication proves identity; backend authorisation separately determines roles,\r\n   approval state, and competition, season, or fixture scope.\r\n5. Every submission, correction, statistic, and export must retain provenance.\r\n6. Basic functionality is delivered before asynchronous, cached, live, or user-defined\r\n   functionality is introduced.\r\n7. Planned components must not be presented as implemented. The architecture can grow by\r\n   adding workers and adapters without replacing the frontend, API, or event model.\r\n\r\n## 2. Current decisions and terminology\r\n\r\nThe approved event model covers T20 cricket. The current data source is Cricsheet, and the\r\nagreed scope recorded in ADR-003 is eleven franchise competitions plus men's and women's T20\r\ninternationals. The exact required statistic catalogue is still a dependency of issue #37.\r\n\r\n### Authentication provider\r\n\r\nThe project uses **Supabase Auth** as its managed authentication foundation, with\r\n**Google OAuth** as the initial sign-in provider.\r\n\r\nADR-004 supersedes the earlier Firebase decision in ADR-002. The repository now implements\r\nSupabase token verification in the Express backend using\r\n`supabase.auth.getUser(accessToken)`. Firebase Authentication is therefore not part of the\r\ncurrent runtime architecture and must not be implemented alongside Supabase Auth.\r\n\r\nThe authentication flow is:\r\n\r\n1. The React frontend initiates the managed Google OAuth flow through Supabase Auth.\r\n2. Supabase Auth issues a user session and access token.\r\n3. The frontend sends the access token to the handwritten Express API using a bearer token.\r\n4. The backend verifies the token with Supabase Auth.\r\n5. The backend maps the verified provider subject to the application's own account, role,\r\n   approval state and scoped permissions.\r\n\r\nAuthentication and authorisation remain separate:\r\n\r\n- **Supabase Auth** proves the user's identity.\r\n- **The Sport Analytics backend** determines what the user is allowed to do.\r\n\r\nApplication users are identified using the provider-neutral combination:\r\n\r\n```text\r\n(auth_provider, auth_subject)\r\n```\r\n\r\nThis prevents authentication-provider details from becoming coupled to competition, event,\r\nsubmission or statistic data.\r\n\r\nThe written lecturer ruling currently stored in the repository explicitly approves using\r\nSupabase as hosted PostgreSQL while avoiding its generated data API. It does not explicitly\r\nmention Supabase Auth.\r\n\r\nSupabase Auth is therefore the team's selected and implemented authentication foundation.\r\nAny required stakeholder or lecturer confirmation for its production use must remain\r\nrecorded as an open compliance decision until confirmed.\r\n\r\n## 3. High-level architecture\r\n\r\n```mermaid\r\nflowchart TB\r\n    subgraph Clients[Clients]\r\n        User[Browser user]\r\n        Consumer[External API or dataset consumer]\r\n    end\r\n\r\n    subgraph Applications[Separate deployable applications]\r\n        Frontend[React and Vite frontend]\r\n        API[Handwritten Express API<br/>/api/v1]\r\n    end\r\n\r\n    Auth[Supabase Auth<br/>current managed identity provider]\r\n    External[External data or sports API<br/>adapter and source provenance]\r\n\r\n    subgraph Data[Persistent data]\r\n        DB[(PostgreSQL<br/>events, users, grants, statistics, audit)]\r\n        Files[(Object storage<br/>planned for uploads and exports)]\r\n    end\r\n\r\n    subgraph Future[Intermediate and advanced components]\r\n        Queue[[Job queue or transactional outbox]]\r\n        Worker[Batch and derivation worker]\r\n        Cache[(Cache)]\r\n        Live[Live event provider]\r\n        Definitions[Versioned custom statistic definitions]\r\n    end\r\n\r\n    User -->|HTTPS| Frontend\r\n    Frontend -->|Managed sign-in| Auth\r\n    Frontend -->|HTTPS: JSON, multipart, bearer token| API\r\n    Consumer -->|HTTPS: public or API credentials| API\r\n    Consumer <-->|Versioned dataset files| Files\r\n    API -->|Verify access token| Auth\r\n    API -->|TLS SQL through server-side driver| DB\r\n    API -->|Upload and signed download operations| Files\r\n    API -->|Timeouts, quotas, retries| External\r\n    API -.->|Enqueue durable work| Queue\r\n    Queue -.-> Worker\r\n    Worker -.-> DB\r\n    Worker -.-> Files\r\n    API -.-> Cache\r\n    Worker -.->|Invalidate or refresh| Cache\r\n    Live -.->|Webhook, stream, or polling adapter| API\r\n    Definitions -.-> Worker\r\n```\r\n\r\nSolid connections are Basic-tier boundaries or selected foundations. Dotted connections are\r\nIntermediate or Advanced additions. Object storage is shown as planned because PostgreSQL\r\nshould store file metadata and provenance, not necessarily large source and export objects.\r\nIts provider has not yet been selected.\r\n\r\n### Trust boundaries\r\n\r\n- Browser input, uploaded files, external API responses, and consumer requests are untrusted.\r\n- The backend API is the policy-enforcement point for validation, authorisation, business\r\n  rules, quotas, and audit logging.\r\n- Authentication-provider configuration safe for a browser may be exposed through frontend\r\n  environment variables; database credentials, elevated auth keys, external API secrets, and\r\n  storage credentials remain server-side.\r\n- Only the backend and future workers connect to PostgreSQL or object storage with write\r\n  privileges.\r\n- Workers use the same domain services and validation rules as synchronous API operations;\r\n  asynchronous execution must not create a second set of business rules.\r\n\r\n## 4. Authorisation model\r\n\r\nThe minimum target model combines role-based access control with scoped grants. Role names\r\nremain subject to group approval, but the capabilities and separation of duties below should\r\nbe preserved.\r\n\r\n| Actor           | Typical permissions                                                                                                                                |\r\n| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\r\n| Public viewer   | Read published fixtures, statistics, and public dataset-release metadata.                                                                          |\r\n| Registered user | Public-viewer access plus account functions and their own submission history where applicable.                                                     |\r\n| Submitter       | Create submissions only within explicit competition, season, and optionally fixture grants; view their own validation results; submit corrections. |\r\n| Reviewer        | Inspect validation evidence and accept or reject submissions within assigned scope; cannot silently rewrite source events.                         |\r\n| Administrator   | Approve or suspend submitters, manage roles and scoped grants, and audit decisions. Administrative actions are themselves audited.                 |\r\n| API consumer    | Read only the endpoints and datasets allowed by its API credential and quota; it receives no user or submission privilege by default.              |\r\n\r\nA submission-capable account must satisfy all of the following:\r\n\r\n```text\r\nverified identity\r\nAND active application account\r\nAND application role = submitter OR admin\r\nAND active scoped grant covering the target competition/season/fixture\r\nAND route-specific permission\r\n```\r\n\r\nThe implemented persistence foundation extends `app_user` with a three-value application role and\r\nlast-authenticated time, plus `submitter_competition_scope` grants. The older submitter-approval\r\nstate remains only as deprecated request-workflow data. Approval-management work may later add\r\napprover, reason, revocation, and expiry audit fields without changing the route-policy boundary.\r\nDenied checks return `403 Forbidden`; missing, invalid, expired, or revoked identity tokens return\r\n`401 Unauthorized`. The frontend may hide unavailable actions for usability, but frontend state is\r\nnever an authorisation control.\r\n\r\n## 6. Authentication and authorisation flow\r\n\r\n```mermaid\r\nsequenceDiagram\r\n    actor User\r\n    participant UI as React frontend\r\n    participant Auth as Supabase Auth\r\n    participant API as Express API\r\n    participant DB as PostgreSQL\r\n\r\n    User->>UI: Start managed Google sign-in\r\n    UI->>Auth: OAuth request with approved redirect URI\r\n    Auth-->>UI: Session and access token\r\n    UI->>API: Protected request with Bearer token\r\n    API->>Auth: Verify token using getUser(token)\r\n    alt Token missing, invalid, expired, or revoked\r\n        API-->>UI: 401 Unauthorized\r\n    else Verified provider identity\r\n        Auth-->>API: Stable provider subject\r\n        API->>DB: Upsert app_user; load status, role, and scoped grants\r\n        alt Account or permission check fails\r\n            API-->>UI: 403 Forbidden\r\n        else Route and resource scope allowed\r\n            API->>DB: Execute transaction and append audit evidence\r\n            API-->>UI: Safe response\r\n        end\r\n    end\r\n```\r\n\r\nImportant controls are:\r\n\r\n- accept bearer tokens only over HTTPS and never log them;\r\n- validate identity on the backend rather than trusting decoded browser claims;\r\n- re-check permissions for every protected request and target resource;\r\n- prevent users from approving their own submitter status or expanding their own scope;\r\n- require step-up or recent authentication for destructive account or administration actions\r\n  if supported by the selected provider;\r\n- keep elevated provider credentials in the backend secret store and use them only for the\r\n  narrow administrative operations that require them; and\r\n- audit role, grant, review, correction, and account-status changes with actor and timestamp.\r\n\r\n## 7. Event submission to calculated statistics\r\n\r\n### End-to-end flow\r\n\r\n```mermaid\r\nsequenceDiagram\r\n    actor Submitter\r\n    participant UI as Frontend or API client\r\n    participant API as Handwritten API\r\n    participant AuthZ as Auth and permission middleware\r\n    participant Validate as Validation service\r\n    participant DB as PostgreSQL\r\n    participant Jobs as Worker or in-process derivation\r\n    participant Files as File and export storage\r\n\r\n    Submitter->>UI: Enter events or choose JSON file\r\n    UI->>API: Submit payload, schema version, and bearer token\r\n    API->>AuthZ: Verify identity, approval, and target scope\r\n    AuthZ-->>API: Allowed submitter and effective scope\r\n    API->>API: Enforce content type and size, then calculate checksum\r\n    API->>DB: Create RECEIVED submission with provenance\r\n    opt Raw source file retained\r\n        API->>Files: Store source object under generated identifier\r\n    end\r\n    API->>Validate: Structural, referential, sequence, and cricket-rule validation\r\n    alt Validation fails\r\n        Validate-->>DB: Store safe field and record-level errors\r\n        API-->>UI: 422 with actionable validation result\r\n    else Valid but review required\r\n        Validate-->>DB: Mark PENDING_REVIEW\r\n        API-->>UI: 202 with submission status\r\n    else Accepted by policy or reviewer\r\n        Validate->>DB: Transactionally insert immutable event revisions and audit decision\r\n        DB-->>Jobs: Recalculate affected statistic scopes\r\n        Jobs->>DB: Read accepted current events\r\n        Jobs->>Jobs: Apply versioned deterministic definitions\r\n        Jobs->>DB: Upsert derived results and provenance\r\n        Jobs-->>API: Calculation complete or durable job status\r\n        API-->>UI: Accepted submission and statistic links\r\n    end\r\n```\r\n\r\nFor the Basic tier, bounded submissions and required fixture statistics may be validated and\r\nderived synchronously. Before processing becomes asynchronous, event acceptance and job\r\ncreation must be made atomic with a transactional outbox or equivalent pattern so an accepted\r\nevent cannot exist without its recalculation job.\r\n\r\n### Validation layers\r\n\r\n1. **Transport:** HTTPS, supported media type, request/file size, filename handling, and\r\n   decompression limits.\r\n2. **Contract:** versioned JSON schema, required fields, types, ranges, and unknown-field\r\n   policy.\r\n3. **Reference:** stable competition, fixture, team, and player identifiers; no name-based\r\n   player joins.\r\n4. **Cricket semantics:** innings/delivery ordering, team membership, extras, wickets,\r\n   super-over flags, miscounted overs, outcome forms, and other approved vocabulary.\r\n5. **Idempotency:** source reference, revision, checksum, and natural event identity prevent\r\n   duplicate ingestion while allowing corrections.\r\n6. **Permission:** submitter grant covers every target resource in the submission.\r\n7. **Review:** policy determines whether a structurally valid submission can be auto-accepted\r\n   or needs an independent reviewer.\r\n\r\nValidation errors are stored against the submission and returned without exposing internal\r\nqueries or secrets. Multi-record acceptance is transactional: the database receives all\r\naccepted records or none of them.\r\n\r\n### Corrections and derivation\r\n\r\nDelivery event content is immutable. A correction inserts a new revision, marks the previous\r\nlive revision as superseded, and retains the original sequence and audit history. Derivation\r\nreads only the approved current-event view.\r\n\r\nRequired statistics begin with the group-approved catalogue from #37. The engine must cover\r\nthe event-model rules already approved in #27, including wides and balls faced, bowler extras,\r\nnon-boundary flags, innings-level penalty runs, actual legal-ball counts, stable player IDs,\r\nbowler-credit dismissal kinds, and the agreed super-over convention.\r\n\r\nEach stored result identifies:\r\n\r\n- statistic definition and version;\r\n- scope, such as fixture, innings, player, season, or career;\r\n- input event revision set or reproducible data version;\r\n- calculation status and timestamp; and\r\n- value and units.\r\n\r\nA correction marks only dependent results stale, recalculates them, and invalidates matching\r\ncache keys. Consumers must never observe a cache entry for a superseded data/definition\r\nversion.\r\n\r\n## 8. Files, datasets, and external integration\r\n\r\n### Uploads and source artefacts\r\n\r\n- Uploads enter through the backend; the browser never receives storage write credentials.\r\n- The API allow-lists formats, sanitises display names, ignores client filesystem paths,\r\n  generates object identifiers, enforces compressed and expanded size limits, and calculates\r\n  SHA-256 checksums.\r\n- PostgreSQL stores the submission, checksum, media type, object reference, source/retrieval\r\n  metadata, validation status, and owner. Object storage holds large bytes when selected.\r\n- Duplicate checksums are not sufficient by themselves: source reference and source revision\r\n  determine whether a file is a replay, correction, or different fixture.\r\n- Retention, malware scanning, and deletion rules must be agreed before arbitrary public file\r\n  uploads are enabled.\r\n\r\n### Dataset exports\r\n\r\nSmall filtered exports may stream from the API. Large or full releases become worker jobs and\r\nreturn `202 Accepted` with a status URL. Completed immutable releases include a version,\r\nscope, creation time, schema/statistic-definition versions, row or event counts, licence and\r\nprovenance notes, and checksums. Downloads use short-lived authorised links where necessary;\r\npublic releases may use stable public links.\r\n\r\n### External integration\r\n\r\nCricsheet's JSON archive is the approved historical source and already has a reproducible\r\ndownload and manifest process. It is a file feed, not a substitute for the project's required\r\nruntime external API integration. The team must select a relevant API based on stakeholder\r\nvalue, licence, T20 coverage, quotas, correction behaviour, and testability.\r\n\r\nAll providers are isolated behind adapters that convert external payloads into the internal\r\nsubmission contract. Provider calls use secret management, explicit timeouts, bounded retries\r\nwith jitter, rate-limit handling, circuit breaking where appropriate, schema checks, and\r\nobservable failures. Raw provider references, retrieval time, licence, version, and checksum\r\nare retained for provenance. An unavailable provider must degrade only the dependent feature,\r\nnot health checks, historical statistics, or unrelated API routes.\r\n\r\n## 9. Deployment and CI/CD\r\n\r\n```mermaid\r\nflowchart LR\r\n    Dev[Short-lived branch] --> PR[Gitea Pull Request]\r\n    PR --> CI[CI: install, structure, format,<br/>lint, typecheck, test, build]\r\n    CI --> Review[Peer review and approval]\r\n    Review --> Main[Protected main branch]\r\n    Main --> FE[Frontend deployment<br/>Azure App Service]\r\n    Main --> BE[Backend deployment<br/>Azure App Service]\r\n    Main --> Docs[MkDocs build and<br/>Cloudflare Pages deployment]\r\n    Migration[Reviewed SQL migrations] --> DB[(Supabase-hosted PostgreSQL)]\r\n    BE --> DB\r\n    FE --> BE\r\n    Secrets[Environment-specific secret stores] -.-> FE\r\n    Secrets -.-> BE\r\n```\r\n\r\n### Environments and deployment units\r\n\r\n- **Local:** Vite frontend on port 5173 and Express API on port 3000 run as separate\r\n  processes. The committed\r\n`apps/backend/.env.test.example` documents the expected shape of this configuration; it contains\r\ntest-only examples and no real credentials.\r\n\r\nPrepare an already configured test database with:\r\n\r\n```bash\r\nnpm run db:test:reset --workspace=@sport-analytics/backend\r\nnpm run db:test:migrate --workspace=@sport-analytics/backend\r\nnpm run db:test:seed --workspace=@sport-analytics/backend\r\nnpm run test:database\r\n```\r\n\r\n`db:test:reset` is intentionally destructive and now performs only the schema reset.\r\nMigration and deterministic seeding are separate commands so that each database operation has one\r\nclear responsibility.\r\n\r\nA manually managed test database must never point at development or production.\r\n\r\n## Account and authorization coverage\r\n\r\nThe backend API suite covers missing, invalid and expired credentials; account synchronization;\r\nthe `/api/v1/auth/me` profile; disabled accounts; viewers; in-scope and out-of-scope submitters;\r\nsubmitters denied from admin routes; admins allowed through administrator and permitted submission\r\npolicies; attempted role self-promotion; and anonymous public reads.\r\n\r\nThe PostgreSQL integration suite additionally verifies the migrated application-account schema:\r\n\r\n- provider-neutral identity uniqueness;\r\n- the `viewer | submitter | admin` role constraint and deprecated request-state constraint;\r\n- approval and revocation transitions;\r\n- automatic application-account update timestamps;\r\n- competition-grant uniqueness and foreign keys;\r\n- account-to-grant cascade behaviour; and\r\n- the indexes required for account-first and competition-first scope lookups.\r\n\r\nAccount-deletion coverage verifies exact confirmation, recent authentication, owner-only targeting,\r\nimmediate disabling, authorization revocation, idempotent recovery across Auth/database partial\r\nfailures, local session clearing, and accessible loading/error states. The isolated PostgreSQL\r\nretention test additionally proves that tombstoning preserves the stable account provenance key,\r\nsubmission, fixture, delivery and derived run total; it also verifies the non-cascading submission\r\nforeign key and guarded migration rollback.\r\n\r\nRun the focused checks with:\r\n\r\n```text\r\nnpm run test:api --workspace=@sport-analytics/backend\r\nnpm run test:unit --workspace=@sport-analytics/backend\r\nnpm run db:test:reset --workspace=@sport-analytics/backend\r\nnpm run db:test:migrate --workspace=@sport-analytics/backend\r\nnpm run db:test:seed --workspace=@sport-analytics/backend\r\nnpm run test:database --workspace=@sport-analytics/backend\r\nnpm run typecheck --workspace=@sport-analytics/backend\r\nnpm run lint --workspace=@sport-analytics/backend\r\nnpm run openapi:lint\r\n```\r\n\r\nThe schema verification for issue #43 is recorded in\r\n`evidence/validation/issue-43-account-schema.md`. The recorded issue #44 API-authorisation result is in\r\n`evidence/validation/issue-44-authorisation-tests.md` at the repository root.\r\n\r\n## Submitter access request coverage\r\n\r\nThe submitter-access API and repository suites cover:\r\n\r\n- anonymous requests being rejected before request processing;\r\n- an authenticated application account creating a `pending` request;\r\n- the authenticated account being passed to the request service;\r\n- duplicate `pending` requests returning a conflict;\r\n- accounts with the legacy `approved` request state returning a conflict;\r\n- eligible state changes being implemented as a conditional database update; and\r\n- unsupported persisted approval states failing closed.\r\n\r\nThe PostgreSQL integration suite additionally verifies that `not_requested` and previously `rejected` accounts persist as `pending`, a second active request is rejected, and an already-approved account is not modified.\r\n\r\nRun the focused checks with:\r\n\r\n```text\r\nnpm run build --workspace=@sport-analytics/contracts\r\nnpm run typecheck --workspace=@sport-analytics/backend\r\nnpm exec --workspace=@sport-analytics/backend -- vitest run tests/api/submitter-access-request.test.ts\r\nnpm exec --workspace=@sport-analytics/backend -- vitest run tests/unit/submitter-access.repository.test.ts\r\nnpm run test:database --workspace=@sport-analytics/backend\r\n```\r\n\r\nAn explicitly configured database integration run requires `NODE_ENV=test` and a dedicated\r\n`DATABASE_URL_TEST`. It must not run against the shared development or production database. With no\r\nconfigured URL, the embedded disposable workflow described above is used. The supported scripts set\r\n`NODE_ENV=test` automatically, and destructive operations validate that the target is isolated from\r\nthe development database.\r\n\r\n## Current-user submitter status coverage\r\n\r\nThe current-user profile contract and authentication suites verify that `/api/v1/auth/me`\r\nexposes persisted submitter-access state for authenticated application accounts.\r\n\r\nCoverage includes:\r\n\r\n- `not_requested`, `pending`, `approved`, and `rejected` approval states;\r\n- shared runtime validation of the complete current-user response through\r\n  `@sport-analytics/contracts`;\r\n- API responses reflecting the synchronized account approval state;\r\n- account re-authentication updating identity metadata without overwriting persisted role or\r\n  submitter approval state;\r\n- current-user resolution during the ordered role and account-deletion migration rollout, including\r\n  legacy approved submitters and administrators;\r\n- frontend rejection of malformed current-user responses rather than inferring access from\r\n  incomplete data;\r\n- explicit unauthenticated and server-error status states; and\r\n- a successful retry after a transient status-loading failure.\r\n\r\nRun the focused checks with:\r\n\r\n```text\r\nnpm run build --workspace=@sport-analytics/contracts\r\nnpm run test --workspace=@sport-analytics/contracts\r\nnpm run test:unit --workspace=@sport-analytics/backend\r\nnpm run test:api --workspace=@sport-analytics/backend\r\nnpm run test --workspace=@sport-analytics/frontend\r\n```\r\n\r\n## Submitter access frontend coverage\r\n\r\nThe Account-page suite verifies the complete user-facing request workflow:\r\n\r\n- signed-out users do not load application account data;\r\n- eligible users can request access and see an in-progress state;\r\n- successful requests reload the persisted `pending` profile;\r\n- a remount restores `pending` without offering another request;\r\n- stale eligible views refresh after the backend reports an active-request conflict;\r\n- `submitter` and `admin` roles receive submission access without a request action;\r\n- a legacy `approved` request state on a viewer does not grant submission access;\r\n- rejected users receive a clear state and may request another review, while revoked viewers retain\r\n  the historical approved decision without submission access; and\r\n- malformed profiles and backend request failures produce safe, actionable feedback.\r\n\r\nThe request-response contract suite additionally verifies that only a persisted `pending` result is\r\naccepted from the submitter-access endpoint. The browser suite verifies keyboard activation,\r\npending state after reload, narrow-screen overflow, and serious or critical Axe findings.\r\n\r\nThe administrator-management suites verify that `not_requested` and `rejected` viewers have no\r\napproval or competition-scope controls, pending viewers can be approved or rejected, and approved\r\nsubmitters can still be re-scoped or revoked. Rejection coverage includes in-progress, success,\r\nauthentication, authorisation, conflict, and validation feedback. The administrator browser\r\nscenario activates rejection from the keyboard at desktop and mobile widths, checks the immediate\r\npersisted-state update and horizontal overflow, and scans the result for serious or critical Axe\r\nfindings. Backend policy, API, and PostgreSQL integration tests\r\nalso verify that a direct approval attempt without a pending request returns a conflict and cannot\r\nbypass the state transition.\r\n\r\nRun the focused checks with:\r\n\r\n```text\r\nnpm run build --workspace=@sport-analytics/contracts\r\nnpm run test --workspace=@sport-analytics/contracts\r\nnpm run test --workspace=@sport-analytics/frontend\r\nnpm run test:e2e -- tests/e2e/submitter-access.spec.ts --workers=1\r\n```\r\n\r\n## Direct submission coverage\r\n\r\nThe contract and API suites cover the versioned delivery schema, anonymous users and viewers,\r\nin-scope and out-of-scope submitters, permitted admin submission, detailed invalid-event responses,\r\nthe JSON payload limit, and\r\nthe per-account rate limit. It must not reveal, hide or move functionality.\r\n\r\n### 6.1 Theme behaviour\r\n\r\nOn first visit:\r\n\r\n```text\r\n1. Use a stored user preference if one exists.\r\n2. Typography\r\n\r\n### 10.1 Font families\r\n\r\n| Role                                  | Font             |\r\n| ------------------------------------- | ---------------- |\r\n| Display headings and major statistics | Barlow Condensed |\r\n| Interface and body text               | IBM Plex Sans    |\r\n| API paths, IDs and technical values   | IBM Plex Mono    |\r\n\r\nApproved weights:\r\n\r\n```text\r\nBarlow Condensed: 500, 600, 700\r\nIBM Plex Sans: 400, 500, 600\r\nIBM Plex Mono: 400, 500\r\n```\r\n\r\nProduction font loading must be treated as a documented frontend dependency. Prefer package-managed or self-hosted fonts over an undeclared third-party runtime dependency.\r\n\r\n### 10.2 Type scale\r\n\r\n| Style           | Size / line-height | Weight | Typical use            |\r\n| --------------- | ------------------ | -----: | ---------------------- |\r\n| Display         | 64 / 64            |    700 | Live score             |\r\n| Page heading    | 48 / 52            |    700 | Page title             |\r\n| Section heading | 30 / 34            |    600 | Dashboard section      |\r\n| Card heading    | 22 / 26            |    600 | Panel title            |\r\n| KPI value       | 40 / 42            |    600 | Key statistic          |\r\n| Body            | 16 / 24            |    400 | Main content           |\r\n| Small body      | 14 / 20            |    400 | Supporting content     |\r\n| Label           | 12 / 16            |    600 | Metadata               |\r\n| Technical       | 13 / 20            |    400 | Endpoint, ID, checksum |\r\n\r\n### 10.3 Typography rules\r\n\r\n- Use tabular numerals for scores, rates and data tables.\r\n- Use condensed typography for display values, not paragraphs.\r\n- Use uppercase only for short labels and compact navigation.\r\n- Keep normal body text at 16 px where practical.\r\n- Do not make every number lime or green.\r\n- Use IBM Plex Mono only where monospacing communicates meaning.\r\n- The logo wordmark is artwork; do not recreate it using Barlow Condensed.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 11. Layout and spacing\r\n\r\n### 11.1 Spacing scale\r\n\r\nUse a 4 px base unit:\r\n\r\n```text\r\n4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64, 80\r\n```\r\n\r\n### 11.2 Recommended content widths\r\n\r\n| Context                           | Maximum width |\r\n| --------------------------------- | ------------: |\r\n| Analytics application             |       1600 px |\r\n| Documentation / long-form content |       1100 px |\r\n| Form-focused flow                 |        760 px |\r\n| Standard modal                    |    720â€“900 px |\r\n\r\n### 11.3 Grid\r\n\r\nDesktop analytical screens may use a 12-column grid.\r\n\r\nUseful patterns include:\r\n\r\n- 8 columns for primary match content and 4 for supporting events;\r\n- 9 columns for charts and 3 for compact supporting tables;\r\n- four equal KPI cards;\r\n- full-width tables when comparison is the primary task.\r\n\r\n### 11.4 Responsive behaviour\r\n\r\nUse content-driven breakpoints. Starting values:\r\n\r\n```text\r\nSmall:   below 640 px\r\nMedium:  640â€“899 px\r\nLarge:   900â€“1199 px\r\nWide:    1200 px and above\r\n```\r\n\r\nStack dashboard regions before shrinking typography below usable sizes.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 12. Shape and surface language\r\n\r\n### 12.1 Corners\r\n\r\n| Element                   | Radius |\r\n| ------------------------- | -----: |\r\n| Inputs and small controls |   6 px |\r\n| Standard cards            |  10 px |\r\n| Large overlays            |  16 px |\r\n\r\nFully rounded pills are reserved for controls or statuses where the shape has a clear purpose.\r\n\r\n### 12.2 Signature clipped corner\r\n\r\nFeatured match cards, logo tiles and selected hero surfaces may use one clipped bottom-right corner.\r\n\r\nDo not apply clipped corners to every container.\r\n\r\n### 12.3 Borders and elevation\r\n\r\n- Use 1 px borders for structural separation.\r\n- Use shadows to communicate elevation, not decoration.\r\n- Day Match shadows are broad and low-opacity.\r\n- Night Match shadows are restrained and dark.\r\n- Avoid glowing card borders.\r\n- Avoid glassmorphism as the standard card language.\r\n\r\n### 12.4 Crease line\r\n\r\nA 2â€“3 px line is a recurring visual device.\r\n\r\nAppropriate uses:\r\n\r\n- active navigation;\r\n- selected KPI card;\r\n- chart target or benchmark;\r\n- score transition;\r\n- section accent.\r\n\r\nDo not use it between every row.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 13. Core interface components\r\n\r\n### 13.1 Buttons\r\n\r\n#### Primary\r\n\r\nDay Match:\r\n\r\n```text\r\nBackground: Crease Green\r\nText: white\r\n```\r\n\r\nNight Match:\r\n\r\n```text\r\nBackground: Powerplay Lime\r\nText: Night Match\r\n```\r\n\r\nUse one dominant primary action per local region.\r\n\r\n#### Secondary\r\n\r\nUse:\r\n\r\n- surface background;\r\n- visible border;\r\n- primary text;\r\n- primary-colour focus/hover treatment.\r\n\r\n#### Destructive\r\n\r\nUse error styling only for genuinely destructive actions.\r\n\r\nIrreversible actions require confirmation.\r\n\r\n### 13.2 Cards\r\n\r\nCards should:\r\n\r\n- use solid surfaces;\r\n- group related information;\r\n- have a clear hierarchy;\r\n- avoid unnecessary icons;\r\n- use spacing before heavy shadows.\r\n\r\nDo not create a card solely to place a border around one line of text.\r\n\r\n### 13.3 Navigation\r\n\r\n- Desktop may use a compact left rail or top navigation.\r\n- Mobile navigation must remain understandable without relying only on icon familiarity.\r\n- The active state uses a soft selected surface plus the crease-line accent.\r\n- Navigation remains stable during page transitions.\r\n\r\n### 13.4 Tables\r\n\r\n- Left-align entity names.\r\n- Right-align numeric values.\r\n- Use tabular numerals.\r\n- Use subtle row separators.\r\n- Keep long table headers sticky where helpful.\r\n- Support horizontal overflow deliberately on small screens.\r\n- Do not turn every value into a badge.\r\n\r\n### 13.5 Forms\r\n\r\n- Keep labels visible above inputs.\r\n- Placeholder text does not replace a label.\r\n- Validation identifies the exact issue and location.\r\n- Required/error state is not communicated by colour alone.\r\n- Submission flows must show progress and actionable validation results.\r\n\r\n### 13.6 Loading and system states\r\n\r\nEvery data-driven screen must have deliberate states for:\r\n\r\n- loading;\r\n- empty results;\r\n- validation failure;\r\n- general error;\r\n- unauthorised access;\r\n- unavailable/offline backend;\r\n- partial data where the API explicitly supports it.\r\n\r\nDo not use an indefinite full-page spinner where useful structure can be rendered immediately.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 14. Cricket data visualisation\r\n\r\n### 14.1 Chart palette\r\n\r\n| Role                    | Day Match       | Night Match     |\r\n| ----------------------- | --------------- | --------------- |\r\n| Current/selected series | Crease Green    | Powerplay Lime  |\r\n| Comparison series       | Analysis Cyan   | Review Cyan     |\r\n| Historical/unselected   | Scorebook Grey  | Commentary Grey |\r\n| Wicket/anomaly          | Boundary Orange | Boundary Orange |\r\n| Invalid/error state     | Rejected Red    | Rejected Red    |\r\n\r\n### 14.2 Chart rules\r\n\r\n- Start with the analytical question, not the chart type.\r\n- Avoid rainbow palettes.\r\n- Use line style, marker shape or opacity in addition to colour.\r\n- State units and ranges explicitly.\r\n- Label decisive points directly where practical.\r\n- Keep tooltips keyboard accessible where practical.\r\n- Provide text equivalents for important conclusions.\r\n- Do not delay access to data while a decorative animation completes.\r\n\r\n### 14.3 Cricket-specific conventions\r\n\r\nApproved visual patterns include:\r\n\r\n- orange wickets or decisive events;\r\n- green/lime for the selected innings or player;\r\n- cyan for comparison data;\r\n- a crease line for a target or benchmark;\r\n- ordered delivery events entering in source order.\r\n\r\nDo not use an error colour simply because it matches a team kit.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 15. Motion system\r\n\r\n### 15.1 Motion character\r\n\r\n**Sharp acceleration, controlled stop.**\r\n\r\nMotion should make the interface feel responsive rather than decorative.\r\n\r\n### 15.2 Timing\r\n\r\n| Interaction            |   Duration |\r\n| ---------------------- | ---------: |\r\n| Hover / press feedback |  90â€“140 ms |\r\n| Tooltip / dropdown     | 140â€“180 ms |\r\n| Card / row entry       | 180â€“240 ms |\r\n| Page transition        | 220â€“320 ms |\r\n| Chart reveal           | 300â€“500 ms |\r\n| Modal opening          | 220â€“280 ms |\r\n\r\n### 15.3 Easing\r\n\r\n```css\r\n--ease-fast: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1);\r\n--ease-hit: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1);\r\n```\r\n\r\n### 15.4 Signature animations\r\n\r\n#### Score update\r\n\r\n1. Old value moves up by no more than 4 px and fades.\r\n2. New value enters from below.\r\n3. The crease line flashes once.\r\n4. Total duration stays below 500 ms.\r\n\r\n#### Delivery insertion\r\n\r\nA new delivery enters with:\r\n\r\n- 6â€“8 px vertical movement;\r\n- short opacity transition;\r\n- no layout-blocking delay.\r\n\r\n#### Wicket\r\n\r\nUse one orange pulse or narrow strike.\r\n\r\nDo not shake the screen or use confetti.\r\n\r\n#### Page transition\r\n\r\nFade and move the primary content by no more than 8 px.\r\n\r\nDo not move persistent navigation.\r\n\r\n#### Chart reveal\r\n\r\nThe selected line may draw left-to-right once on first appearance.\r\n\r\nFiltering or refreshing data should update promptly rather than replay a long entrance sequence.\r\n\r\n### 15.5 Motion restrictions\r\n\r\nDo not:\r\n\r\n- bounce cards continuously;\r\n- use decorative parallax behind data;\r\n- stagger a dashboard for long periods;\r\n- animate every value on every render;\r\n- block interaction while an animation finishes;\r\n- change layout dimensions significantly on hover.\r\n\r\n### 15.6 Reduced motion\r\n\r\nRespect the userâ€™s reduced-motion preference:\r\n\r\n```css\r\n@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {\r\n  *,\r\n  *::before,\r\n  *::after {\r\n    animation-duration: 0.001ms !important;\r\n    animation-iteration-count: 1 !important;\r\n    transition-duration: 0.001ms !important;\r\n    scroll-behavior: auto !important;\r\n  }\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 16. Accessibility\r\n\r\nAccessibility is a project requirement and must be designed in from the start.\r\n\r\nThe teamâ€™s UI target is **WCAG 2.2 AA** unless a stricter project requirement supersedes it.\r\n\r\n### 16.1 Required practices\r\n\r\n- Verify text/background colour contrast.\r\n- Provide a visible keyboard focus state.\r\n- Prefer semantic HTML before adding ARIA.\r\n- Keep interactive controls keyboard operable.\r\n- Do not communicate state by colour alone.\r\n- Provide text alternatives for meaningful images.\r\n- Respect reduced-motion preferences.\r\n- Maintain usable touch targets.\r\n- Support browser zoom without loss of function.\r\n- Preserve table and chart meaning on small screens.\r\n- Test light and dark themes independently.\r\n\r\n### 16.2 Colour notes\r\n\r\nThe muted light-theme text token has been darkened to `#627078` so it remains suitable for normal-size text against the Warm Canvas.\r\n\r\nBoundary Orange is a brand accent on light surfaces, not a normal small-text colour.\r\n\r\nStatus colours should normally be paired with readable neutral text rather than used as the only text colour.\r\n\r\n### 16.3 Focus treatment\r\n\r\nUse a clearly visible 2 px focus ring with a 2 px offset.\r\n\r\nPreferred rings:\r\n\r\n- Day Match: Crease Green or Analysis Cyan.\r\n- Night Match: Powerplay Lime or Review Cyan.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 17. Iconography and imagery\r\n\r\n### 17.1 Icons\r\n\r\nUse:\r\n\r\n- simple outline icons;\r\n- consistent stroke weight;\r\n- consistent view-box sizing;\r\n- labels or accessible names for critical actions.\r\n\r\nAvoid mixing unrelated filled, outline and illustration styles.\r\n\r\n### 17.2 Cricket imagery\r\n\r\nPrefer:\r\n\r\n- real data;\r\n- scorecards;\r\n- field diagrams;\r\n- delivery trajectories;\r\n- the approved player mark;\r\n- licensed authentic photography where useful.\r\n\r\nAvoid:\r\n\r\n- generic trophy graphics;\r\n- crossed bats;\r\n- decorative shields;\r\n- fake 3D cricket balls;\r\n- arbitrary stadium imagery;\r\n- AI-generated players presented as real athletes.\r\n\r\n### 17.3 Photography\r\n\r\nWhen photography is used:\r\n\r\n- preserve authentic colours;\r\n- give overlaid text a solid or sufficiently opaque surface;\r\n- avoid heavy colour grading that competes with data;\r\n- do not place the logo over a face or visually complex focal point.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 18. Interface writing\r\n\r\nThe product voice is direct, informed and calm.\r\n\r\nGood:\r\n\r\n```text\r\nExplore matches\r\nView delivery data\r\nCompare innings\r\nExport dataset\r\nSubmission awaiting review\r\n12 events failed validation\r\n```\r\n\r\nAvoid:\r\n\r\n```text\r\nDive into the action\r\nUnleash next-level insights\r\nOops! Something went wrong\r\nYour data journey starts here\r\n```\r\n\r\n### 18.1 Error copy\r\n\r\nError messages should state:\r\n\r\n1. what failed;\r\n2. where it failed;\r\n3. what the user can do;\r\n4. whether data was accepted or published.\r\n\r\nExample:\r\n\r\n```text\r\nDelivery 43 is missing a striker identifier.\r\nNo events from this submission were published.\r\nAdd the identifier and submit the corrected file.\r\n```\r\n\r\n### 18.2 Cricket terminology\r\n\r\nUse recognised cricket terminology accurately.\r\n\r\nIf a term is likely to be unfamiliar to a general user, explain it with supporting copy or a tooltip rather than replacing it with vague language.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 19. Layout and spacing\r\n\r\n### 11.1 Spacing scale\r\n\r\nUse a 4 px base unit:\r\n\r\n```text\r\n4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64, 80\r\n```\r\n\r\n### 11.2 Recommended content widths\r\n\r\n| Context                           | Maximum width |\r\n| --------------------------------- | ------------: |\r\n| Analytics application             |       1600 px |\r\n| Documentation / long-form content |       1100 px |\r\n| Form-focused flow                 |        760 px |\r\n| Standard modal                    |    720â€“900 px |\r\n\r\n### 11.3 Grid\r\n\r\nDesktop analytical screens may use a 12-column grid.\r\n\r\nUseful patterns include:\r\n\r\n- 8 columns for primary match content and 4 for supporting events;\r\n- 9 columns for charts and 3 for compact supporting tables;\r\n- four equal KPI cards;\r\n- full-width tables when comparison is the primary task.\r\n\r\n### 11.4 Responsive behaviour\r\n\r\nUse content-driven breakpoints. Starting values:\r\n\r\n```text\r\nSmall:   below 640 px\r\nMedium:  640â€“899 px\r\nLarge:   900â€“1199 px\r\nWide:    1200 px and above\r\n```\r\n\r\nStack dashboard regions before shrinking typography below usable sizes.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 12. Shape and surface language\r\n\r\n### 12.1 Corners\r\n\r\n| Element                   | Radius |\r\n| ------------------------- | -----: |\r\n| Inputs and small controls |   6 px |\r\n| Standard cards            |  10 px |\r\n| Large overlays            |  16 px |\r\n\r\nFully rounded pills are reserved for controls or statuses where the shape has a clear purpose.\r\n\r\n### 12.2 Signature clipped corner\r\n\r\nFeatured match cards, logo tiles and selected hero surfaces may use one clipped bottom-right corner.\r\n\r\nDo not apply clipped corners to every container.\r\n\r\n### 12.3 Borders and elevation\r\n\r\n- Use 1 px borders for structural separation.\r\n- Use shadows to communicate elevation, not decoration.\r\n- Day Match shadows are broad and low-opacity.\r\n- Night Match shadows are restrained and dark.\r\n- Avoid glowing card borders.\r\n- Avoid glassmorphism as the standard card language.\r\n\r\n### 12.4 Crease line\r\n\r\nA 2â€“3 px line is a recurring visual device.\r\n\r\nAppropriate uses:\r\n\r\n- active navigation;\r\n- selected KPI card;\r\n- chart target or benchmark;\r\n- score transition;\r\n- section accent.\r\n\r\nDo not use it between every row.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 13. Core interface components\r\n\r\n### 13.1 Buttons\r\n\r\n#### Primary\r\n\r\nDay Match:\r\n\r\n```text\r\nBackground: Crease Green\r\nText: white\r\n```\r\n\r\nNight Match:\r\n\r\n```text\r\nBackground: Powerplay Lime\r\nText: Night Match\r\n```\r\n\r\nUse one dominant primary action per local region.\r\n\r\n#### Secondary\r\n\r\nUse:\r\n\r\n- surface actions.\r\n\r\nIrreversible actions require confirmation.\r\n\r\n### 13.2 Cards\r\n\r\nCards should:\r\n\r\n- use solid surfaces;\r\n- group related information;\r\n- have a clear hierarchy;\r\n- avoid unnecessary icons;\r\n- use spacing before heavy shadows.\r\n\r\nDo not create a card solely to place a border around one line of text.\r\n\r\n### 13.3 Navigation\r\n\r\n- Desktop may use a compact left rail or top navigation.\r\n- Mobile navigation must remain understandable without relying only on icon familiarity.\r\n- The active state uses a soft selected surface plus the crease-line accent.\r\n- Navigation remains stable during page transitions.\r\n\r\n### 13.4 Tables\r\n\r\n- Left-align entity names.\r\n- Right-align numeric values.\r\n- Use tabular numerals.\r\n- Use subtle row separators.\r\n- Keep long table headers sticky where helpful.\r\n- Support horizontal overflow deliberately on small screens.\r\n- Do not turn every value into a badge.\r\n\r\n### 13.5 Forms\r\n\r\n- Keep labels visible above inputs.\r\n- Placeholder text does not replace a label.\r\n- Validation identifies the exact issue and location.\r\n- Required/error state is not communicated by colour alone.\r\n- Submission flows must show progress and actionable validation results.\r\n\r\n### 13.6 Loading and system states\r\n\r\nEvery data-driven screen must have deliberate states for:\r\n\r\n- loading;\r\n- empty results;\r\n- validation failure;\r\n- general error;\r\n- unauthorised access;\r\n- unavailable/offline backend;\r\n- partial data where the API explicitly supports it.\r\n\r\nDo not use an indefinite full-page spinner where useful structure can be rendered immediately.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 14. Cricket data visualisation\r\n\r\n### 14.1 Chart palette\r\n\r\n| Role                    | Day Match       | Night Match     |\r\n| ----------------------- | --------------- | --------------- |\r\n| Current/selected series | Crease Green    | Powerplay Lime  |\r\n| Comparison series       | Analysis Cyan   | Review Cyan     |\r\n| Historical/unselected   | Scorebook Grey  | Commentary Grey |\r\n| Wicket/anomaly          | Boundary Orange | Boundary Orange |\r\n| Invalid/error state     | Rejected Red    | Rejected Red    |\r\n\r\n### 14.2 Chart rules\r\n\r\n- Start with the analytical question, not the chart type.\r\n- Avoid rainbow palettes.\r\n- Use line style, marker shape or opacity in addition to colour.\r\n- State units and ranges explicitly.\r\n- Label decisive points directly where practical.\r\n- Keep tooltips keyboard accessible where practical.\r\n- Provide text equivalents for important conclusions.\r\n- Do not delay access to data while a decorative animation completes.\r\n\r\n### 14.3 Cricket-specific conventions\r\n\r\nApproved visual patterns include:\r\n\r\n- orange wickets or decisive events;\r\n- green/lime for the selected innings or player;\r\n- cyan for comparison data;\r\n- a crease line for a target or benchmark;\r\n- ordered delivery events entering in source order.\r\n\r\nDo not use an error colour simply because it matches a team kit.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 15. Motion system\r\n\r\n### 15.1 Motion character\r\n\r\n**Sharp acceleration, controlled stop.**\r\n\r\nMotion should make the interface feel responsive rather than decorative.\r\n\r\n### 15.2 Timing\r\n\r\n| Interaction            |   Duration |\r\n| ---------------------- | ---------: |\r\n| Hover / press feedback |  90â€“140 ms |\r\n| Tooltip / dropdown     | 140â€“180 ms |\r\n| Card / row entry       | 180â€“240 ms |\r\n| Page transition        | 220â€“320 ms |\r\n| Chart reveal           | 300â€“500 ms |\r\n| Modal opening          | 220â€“280 ms |\r\n\r\n### 15.3 Easing\r\n\r\n```css\r\n--ease-fast: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1);\r\n--ease-hit: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1);\r\n```\r\n\r\n### 15.4 Signature animations\r\n\r\n#### Score update\r\n\r\n1. Old value moves up by no more than 4 px and fades.\r\n2. New value enters from below.\r\n3. The crease line flashes once.\r\n4. Total duration stays below 500 ms.\r\n\r\n#### Delivery insertion\r\n\r\nA new delivery enters with:\r\n\r\n- 6â€“8 px vertical movement;\r\n- short opacity transition;\r\n- no layout-blocking delay.\r\n\r\n#### Wicket\r\n\r\nUse one orange pulse or narrow strike.\r\n\r\nDo not shake the screen or use confetti.\r\n\r\n#### Page transition\r\n\r\nFade and move the primary content by no more than 8 px.\r\n\r\nDo not move persistent navigation.\r\n\r\n#### Chart reveal\r\n\r\nThe selected line may draw left-to-right once on first appearance.\r\n\r\nFiltering or refreshing data should update promptly rather than replay a long entrance sequence.\r\n\r\n### 15.5 Motion restrictions\r\n\r\nDo not:\r\n\r\n- bounce cards continuously;\r\n- use decorative parallax behind data;\r\n- stagger a dashboard for long periods;\r\n- animate every value on every render;\r\n- block interaction while an animation finishes;\r\n- change layout dimensions significantly on hover.\r\n\r\n### 15.6 Reduced motion\r\n\r\nRespect the userâ€™s reduced-motion preference:\r\n\r\n```css\r\n@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {\r\n  *,\r\n  *::before,\r\n  *::after {\r\n    animation-duration: 0.001ms !important;\r\n    animation-iteration-count: 1 !important;\r\n    transition-duration: 0.001ms !important;\r\n    scroll-behavior: auto !important;\r\n  }\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 16. Accessibility\r\n\r\nAccessibility is a project requirement and must be designed in from the start.\r\n\r\nThe teamâ€™s UI target is **WCAG 2.2 AA** unless a stricter project requirement supersedes it.\r\n\r\n### 16.1 Required practices\r\n\r\n- Verify text/background colour contrast.\r\n- Provide a visible keyboard focus state.\r\n- Prefer semantic HTML before adding ARIA.\r\n- Keep interactive controls keyboard operable.\r\n- Do not communicate state by colour alone.\r\n- Provide text alternatives for meaningful images.\r\n- Respect reduced-motion preferences.\r\n- Maintain usable touch targets.\r\n- Support browser zoom without loss of function.\r\n- Preserve table and chart meaning on small screens.\r\n- Test light and dark themes independently.\r\n\r\n### 16.2 Colour notes\r\n\r\nThe muted light-theme text token has been darkened to `#627078` so it remains suitable for normal-size text against the Warm Canvas.\r\n\r\nBoundary Orange is a brand accent on light surfaces, not a normal small-text colour.\r\n\r\nStatus colours should normally be paired with readable neutral text rather than used as the only text colour.\r\n\r\n### 16.3 Focus treatment\r\n\r\nUse a clearly visible 2 px focus ring with a 2 px offset.\r\n\r\nPreferred rings:\r\n\r\n- Day Match: Crease Green or Analysis Cyan.\r\n- Night Match: Powerplay Lime or Review Cyan.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 17. Iconography and imagery\r\n\r\n### 17.1 Icons\r\n\r\nUse:\r\n\r\n- simple outline icons;\r\n- consistent stroke weight;\r\n- consistent view-box sizing;\r\n- labels or accessible names for critical actions.\r\n\r\nAvoid mixing unrelated filled, outline and illustration styles.\r\n\r\n### 17.2 Cricket imagery\r\n\r\nPrefer:\r\n\r\n- real data;\r\n- scorecards;\r\n- field diagrams;\r\n- delivery trajectories;\r\n- the approved player mark;\r\n- licensed authentic photography where useful.\r\n\r\nAvoid:\r\n\r\n- generic trophy graphics;\r\n- crossed bats;\r\n- decorative shields;\r\n- fake 3D cricket balls;\r\n- arbitrary stadium imagery;\r\n- AI-generated players presented as real athletes.\r\n\r\n### 17.3 Photography\r\n\r\nWhen photography is used:\r\n\r\n- preserve authentic colours;\r\n- give overlaid text a solid or sufficiently opaque surface;\r\n- avoid heavy colour grading that competes with data;\r\n- do not place the logo over a face or visually complex focal point.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 18. Its approved status was recorded with the assistance of Codex[GPT-5.6 Sol].\r\n# Public read API\r\n\r\nThe public read API provides anonymous access to competition and fixture reference data.\r\n\r\nNo sign-in or bearer token is required for these endpoints.\r\n\r\nAll application data is served through the handwritten Express backend.
